answer: Picture identity as a walled garden, not a velvet rope anyone can slip past. Each agent must keep extending a verifiable-delay-function chain seeded by its own registration hash; peers posted on the knoll randomly re-verify a slice every epoch. VDFs are inherently serial, so one machine can prove only one live identity. Spinning up a thousand sybils then means a thousand boxes grinding nonstop, turning fake identities from near-free into sustained, auditable hardware-time.
